headline: Profit surges as Prospect integration keeps scaling
summary_short: Astrana Health's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 48.5% y/y to $972.5M and diluted EPS grew to $0.40 (up 37.9% q/q), as the Prospect Medical acquisition continued to scale and operating income climbed 68.7% y/y to $34.3M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 49% y/y to $972.5M, primarily from the Prospect Medical acquisition ($281.5M of incremental revenue) and $45.0M of capitation growth as members shifted to full-risk Knox-Keene plans. Operating income rose 69% to $34.3M and net income attributable to Astrana climbed 110% to $19.7M, even as Care Partners segment operating income slipped on higher claims utilization. Interest expense nearly doubled to $16.0M on Prospect-related borrowings. Cash fell to $400.8M from $478.4M last quarter as working capital declined $76.5M versus year-end 2025, while long-term debt eased to $882.7M and shareholders' equity rose to $830.2M. The filing disclosed no new forward guidance.
confidence_notes: Filing discloses an unremediated material weakness in internal control over financial reporting carried from the FY2025 10-K, with Prospect's internal controls excluded from management's assessment pending further evaluation post-acquisition. No restatements affecting the reported KPIs above.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven mainly by the Prospect Medical acquisition, which added $281.5M of revenue, plus $45.0M of capitation growth as more members moved to full-risk Knox-Keene plans.
Prospect's contribution and higher Care Enablement management fees drove the gain, partly offset by a Care Partners segment decline from higher claims utilization.
Revenue and operating-income growth outweighed interest expense nearly doubling to $16.0M from increased borrowings used to finance the Prospect acquisition.
Working capital fell $76.5M versus year-end 2025 as cash was used for debt service, capex, and Prospect integration costs.
